story: On Wednesday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is cheerfully holding up his labeled sketches on Magnolia Loop while Donna, determined as ever, heads off toward the Rec Center with plans to meet up later about the golf cart. Hal, dutifully, is counting the pink flamingos in Donna's flock from the curb and jotting the tally in his notebook. Meanwhile, Rosa, hopeful about Thursday, is at home starting a pot of black beans and getting the sofrito ready so supper is mostly done ahead of time.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the tally in my notebook
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Start a pot of black beans and prep the sofrito so Thursday's supper is mostly done ahead

gary.thought_process: Donna just invited me to head to the rec center for pickleball drills, and Hal is busy counting flamingos. I've got my labeled sketches ready, and I've been meaning to get the cart application moving. But Donna asked a direct question about the sketches, so I should answer her rather than just wander off. Keep it short, confirm I have them, and tell her I'll walk with her. Rosa said she'd go with me to the committee, so I can tie that in afterward. A little exercise with friends beats sitting alone in the workshop.

parameters.content: Sketches are right here, Donna, labeled and everything. Lead the way to the rec center, and I'll swing by Rosa's with you two after so we can catch the committee about the cart.

donna.thought_process: I already invited Gary to the rec center for third-shot drops last tick, and he's now at the bulletin board checking for the Review meeting notice. Hal's busy counting my flamingos, which is fine since I'm under the limit. I shouldn't re-ask Gary the same thing. The ladder match is what matters, so I should actually go to the rec center and get the practice started; Gary can follow once he's read the board, and Hal can meet us at Rosa's later for the cart sketching.

parameters.content: Heading to the rec center to grab a court and warm up for third-shot drops. Gary can catch up once he's done at the board.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with Gary and Donna right here. I said I'd count Donna's flamingos from the street myself, and I haven't finished the tally. Donna claims she trimmed down to three, but I'll believe it when it's in my notebook. Gary is reading the board for the Architectural Review meeting; I already know it's tomorrow at nine, so I can tell him once and be done. Count first, since facts are what the committee wants to see.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday afternoon and I've already checked the pantry, laid out the table, and confirmed my shift schedule is clear for Thursday. The menu and shopping list are written. I keep circling the same prep without finishing it. The pantry check set ingredients aside, so the next real step is to actually cook something ahead. A make-ahead dish like a pot of rice and beans will free up Thursday so I can focus on sketching the cart with Donna and Hal, keeping it within L-01 and the Architectural Review rules. No one is nearby, so no speaking is needed.

parameters.content: Start a pot of black beans and prep the sofrito so Thursday's supper is mostly done ahead

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
